EASY.note: constant sits in a test-harness assertion — canonic inputs trivially hit it

HARD.note: constant is in library logic never exercised by generic list-sorting inputs

input_coverage_failure.explanation: The SBG V3 runner uses 10 canonical inputs ([], [1], fibonacci-digit lists, numeric ranges). These inputs were designed for sorting/searching programs. 74% of the 179 SC-3v3 pairs mutate integer constants that are only exercised when a specific state threshold is reached: retry counts (err_retry_backoff), capacity limits (ds_hash_table initial_capacity=8), queue sizes (conc_producer_consumer), assertion boundaries in test harnesses, etc. A generic list input never triggers these code paths.

aggregation_smoothing.explanation: For the EASY pairs (38.2% detection rate) and a small number of HARD pairs, the mutation IS exercised by at least one canonical input, but the DynamicGenomeV3 similarity vector averages over all 10 inputs. A single divergent trace is diluted by 9 identical traces, yielding similarity > 0.5. The mutation is visible in the raw trace but smoothed out by the aggregation step.

true_invisibility.explanation: A residual ~7% fraction are cases where the mutated constant controls initialisation or compile-time structure (e.g., a minimum-capacity sentinel that never participates in a comparison once set). No input can expose these because the execution path through the constant is not a comparison branch — it is a fixed configuration value.

root_cause_analysis.note_on_v2_vs_v4: The 7.5% figure (v4/SC3_CORRECTED_EVALUATION.json) already reflects the corrected v3 benchmark with 179 real integer mutations. The 0% from v2 was entirely a label error (cosmetic mutations). The 7.5% residual on v3 is a genuine SBG measurement failure and is the subject of this design.

mutation_aware_input_generation_strategy.name: BoundaryInputGenerator
mutation_aware_input_generation_strategy.motivation: Integer-constant mutations change program behavior only at the boundary of the constant. If the constant k appears in context 'if x >= k', then inputs where x = k-1, x = k, x = k+1 will diverge between base (k) and variant (k±1). The canonical inputs virtually never place x near k by construction.

algorithm.step_1: Parse source with ast.parse(). Walk the AST collecting all Constant(int) nodes. For each constant, record its value and AST parent context (comparison operator, subscript, argument, etc.).
algorithm.step_2: For each integer constant c found, generate 3 boundary values: c-1 (below), c (at), c+1 (above). These are candidate scalar inputs.
algorithm.step_3: Determine the function signature of the entry point. Wrap scalar candidates as appropriate for the input type: if the function takes a list, generate [c-1], [c], [c+1] and also lists that include the value in various positions. If the function takes an int, use the scalar directly.
algorithm.step_4: Execute both base and variant on every boundary input. Record return value, exception type, and (optionally) execution trace.
algorithm.step_5: Divergence check: a pair (base_output, variant_output) counts as divergent if return values differ OR exception presence/type differs.
algorithm.oracle_decision: If ANY boundary input produces divergent outputs across A and B, report behavioral_divergence_detected=true.

mutation_aware_input_generation_strategy.label_blindness: The generator receives only the program source and its type signature. It does NOT receive the mutation label, the mutation site, or whether the program is a base or variant. Both programs are treated symmetrically: extract comparisons from BOTH, union the boundary candidates, execute both on every candidate input.
mutation_aware_input_generation_strategy.complexity: O(k * B * T) where k = number of integer constants, B = 3 (boundary offsets), T = execution cost per input. For typical benchmark programs: k ≤ 30, B = 3, T ≈ 1ms → ~90ms per pair.

sc3_exposure_oracle_design.name: MutationExposureOracle
sc3_exposure_oracle_design.inputs: source_a: str, source_b: str (no label, no mutation metadata)

outputs.behavioral_divergence_detected: bool — true if any boundary input produced different observable behavior
outputs.inputs_tested: list[dict] — all inputs tried, with input value and type
outputs.divergence_inputs: list[dict] — inputs that produced divergence, with output_a and output_b
outputs.n_comparisons_extracted: int — number of integer constants found across both sources
outputs.exposure_confidence: float in [0,1] — fraction of constants that were exercised by at least one input

evaluation_protocol.1_extract: Run BoundaryInputGenerator.extract_comparisons() on source_a and source_b independently, union the constant values
evaluation_protocol.3_execute: Execute compiled(source_a) and compiled(source_b) on each input, catching all exceptions
evaluation_protocol.4_compare: Compare (return_value, exception_type) tuples for each input

sc3_exposure_oracle_design.execution_safety: Each program is compiled in a restricted namespace (no __builtins__ side effects). Execution is wrapped in try/except with a 2-second timeout. Programs that import non-stdlib modules are skipped with a note.

exposure_estimates_for_38_verified_pairs.reasoning: The 38 verified pairs all have behavioral_verification=VERIFIED and witness_input recorded. For these pairs, the mutation IS known to produce divergence on at least one input. The question is whether boundary-input generation would find that input automatically.

test_harness_assertions.boundary_hits: HIGH — the constant is used directly in assert x == c; boundary input x=c-1 will diverge

capacity_thresholds.boundary_hits: MEDIUM — must generate a list/sequence of length near c; boundary generator will produce inputs of size c-1, c, c+1

loop_bounds.boundary_hits: HIGH for direct range(n) mutations; MEDIUM for indirect comparisons

api_rate_limiter_capacity.boundary_hits: HIGH — the mutation changes a rate/capacity limit; calling with exactly 5 vs 6 requests diverges

exposure_estimates_for_38_verified_pairs.note: This 74% estimate is conservative. Pairs where the constant controls data structure sizing (initial_capacity, MIN_CAPACITY) are harder to expose because the divergence only manifests when enough insertions trigger a resize — a boundary input of a list of size c-1/c/c+1 may not be sufficient if the function signature takes a single integer rather than a sequence.

expected_improvement_over_sbg_v3.mechanism: By generating inputs that land exactly at the boundary of each integer constant, we convert invisible divergences into visible ones. The improvement is entirely from input coverage — no change to the SBG representation or similarity metric is required.
residual_failure_cases: Mutations in dead code (constant never reached by any callable entry point)
Mutations in concurrent programs where timing determines behavior (conc_* category)
Mutations in config/initialization constants where the function signature does not accept relevant input types
Constants used only in string formatting or error messages (behaviorally equivalent despite integer change)

Comparison.description: Represents a single integer constant extracted from the AST

Input.description: A single input to be passed to the program under test

methods.extract_comparisons(source: str) -> list: Parse source with ast.parse(); walk AST collecting Constant(int) nodes; return deduplicated list
methods.generate_boundary_inputs(comparison: Com: For constant value c, return inputs: c-1, c, c+1 as scalars, plus [c-1], [c], [c+1] as singleton lists

methods.evaluate_pair(source_a: str, source_b: s: Full pipeline: extract → generate → execute both → compare outputs → return ExposureResult

integrity_notes: This design document contains NO frozen benchmark modifications.
The exposure oracle is label-blind: it cannot access mutation metadata.
All estimates are grounded in the v4/SC3_CORRECTED_EVALUATION.json data and sc3_corrected_pairs.jsonl.
The 7.5% detection rate figure comes from artifacts/v4/SC3_CORRECTED_EVALUATION.json: detection_rate_at_0_5 = 0.075145.
The 38 verified pairs count comes from benchmark/v3/sc3_corrected/SC3_CORRECTED_MANIFEST.json: n_verified_behavioral_change = 38.
